the cytomegalovirus (CMV) promoter of the CDBF vector drives constitutive BFP (blue fluorescence protein) expression and by virtue of the splice donor (SD) sequence, an overexpressed FLAG-tagged fusion of the targeted gene.
Human A375 melanoma cells containing a β-catenin-driven GFP (green fluorescent protein) transcriptional reporter were transduced with CDBF lentivirus.
Fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) was used to isolate BFP+/GFP+ (Wnt active) or BFP+/GFP- (Wnt inactive) A375 cells.
A BFP only population was also sorted as a negative control.
The FOXP1 transcription factor ranked as the top screen hit, as determined by spectral count abundance and the CompPASS WD-score across four biological replicate screens.

Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The proteomics experiment described is a gain-of-function screen using a CD-tagging (CDBF) lentiviral system to identify proteins that activate Wnt signaling. The primary biological variable is the overexpression of random genes (via the viral library) that leads to a Wnt-active phenotype (GFP+). The MS analysis specifically compares the FLAG-tagged proteins enriched in the Wnt-active population versus the Wnt-inactive/control population.
